L7·N3173unmasked layer
Fires at sentence-boundary punctuation — the period (or period+newline, and occasionally a comma) that closes a clause before a new sentence begins, peaking when the period is fused directly to the next capitalized word (".Y"); it's driven by the punctuation-boundary position rather than any topic, and the same ".\n" token is strongly *negative* in casual/first-person chatty prose.

This neuron is broadly (mid-level) active across ordinary running prose, with its peak landing on the short function word — usually "the", also "for"/"called" — that immediately introduces a specific named noun phrase or item (e.g. "the great memoirs", "the Committee on Appropriations", "planned for June 3", "It's called friluftsliv"), plus digits in phone-number strings; it is a low-selectivity, position-of-introducer neuron rather than a semantic one.
